articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities, Issues New General Licenses, and Amends FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. This action targets entities and individuals deemed to be involved in illicit activities supporting the Iranian regime.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also issued new Iran-related General Licenses and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide guidance on the scope of the new measures and permissible transactions. The details of the designated entities and the specific authorizations under the General Licenses were not immediately released but are expected to clarify compliance obligations for U.S. persons.

Additionally, the announcement included removals of designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions efforts in those regions. Further, Russia-related General Licenses were also issued, suggesting ongoing adjustments to the sanctions landscape concerning Moscow.

articles.headline: PAIPA Designations Imposed with Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026. These designations aim to combat the theft of American intellectual property by foreign actors.

Alongside the designations, OFAC issued associated General Licenses to mitigate unintended consequences and provide clarity for legitimate transactions. The specific individuals and entities targeted by these PAIPA designations, and the scope of the accompanying General Licenses, were detailed in the official announcement.
This action underscores the U.S. government's continued commitment to safeguarding American innovation and technology from illicit acquisition and exploitation.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an amendment to a Venezuela-related General License and an associated Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) on October 16, 2026. This adjustment aims to refine existing sanctions policy concerning Venezuela.

The amendment likely provides updated guidance or expands the scope of permissible activities under the specified General License, offering more clarity to individuals and entities engaging in certain transactions involving Venezuela. The accompanying FAQ further elaborates on the interpretation and application of the amended license.
Such modifications are part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to ensure that sanctions remain effective while minimizing undue burdens on legitimate humanitarian or commercial activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran and Cuba Designations, Issues New and Amended General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations related to Iran and a specific designation concerning Cuba on October 15, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities involved in activities contrary to U.S. foreign policy objectives.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses, along with updated Frequently Asked Questions. These accompanying measures are intended to provide guidance and authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by the new sanctions.
The designations against Iran are part of ongoing efforts to counter the regime's destabilizing activities, while the Cuba designation reflects continued pressure on the Cuban government.

articles.headline: Venezuela-Related Designation Removed by OFAC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation on October 14, 2026. This action indicates a recalibration of sanctions against individuals or entities previously targeted under the Venezuela sanctions program.

Designation removals typically occur when the sanctioned party meets certain criteria, such as demonstrating a change in behavior, providing additional information, or when the U.S. government determines that the designation no longer serves its policy objectives.
Such removals can signal a potential shift in diplomatic or economic engagement with Venezuela, or a targeted adjustment based on specific circumstances related to the delisted entity.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities on October 13, 2026. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to disrupt illicit networks that pose threats to U.S. national security.

The designations aim to sever financial and material support for drug trafficking organizations and terrorist groups globally. By blocking the assets of these designated parties, OFAC seeks to limit their ability to operate and finance their illicit operations.
These measures underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating transnational crime and terrorism through financial sanctions and international cooperation.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Issues ICC Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026, resolving alleged violations of U.S. sanctions programs. The details of the violations and the terms of the settlement were made public, highlighting the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.

In a separate action on the same date, OFAC also announced a designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued associated General Licenses. This designation reflects U.S. policy concerning the ICC and aims to manage the implications of the designation through specific authorizations.
Furthermore, the announcement included a Burma-related designation removal, indicating a targeted adjustment to sanctions policy concerning Myanmar.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026. This action provides specific authorizations for certain transactions involving Russia that would otherwise be prohibited under existing sanctions programs.

General Licenses are often issued to clarify the scope of sanctions, facilitate humanitarian aid, or allow for certain routine commercial activities that are not intended to be disrupted by broader sanctions. The details of this new license specify the types of transactions and parties covered.
This issuance reflects OFAC's ongoing management of the Russia sanctions program, aiming to balance the effectiveness of sanctions with practical considerations for various sectors.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities, Issues New Iran-Related and Amended Russia-Related General Licenses

In conjunction with these actions, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License, providing specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited. Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License was amended, indicating adjustments to the scope of permissible activities concerning Russia.
These measures highlight OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, continuously adapting to geopolitical developments and refining the implementation of its various programs.

articles.headline: OCC Advances U.S. Digital Asset Leadership with Final Rule to Implement GENIUS Act
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced on October 21, 2026, a final rule to implement the GENIUS Act, advancing U.S. digital asset leadership. This rule is expected to provide a clearer regulatory framework for national banks and federal savings associations engaging with digital assets.

The GENIUS Act aims to foster innovation in the financial sector while ensuring appropriate risk management and consumer protection in the rapidly evolving digital asset space. The OCC's final rule is a significant step towards integrating digital assets into the traditional banking system.

This development underscores the OCC's commitment to maintaining the competitiveness of the U.S. financial system in the digital age and providing regulatory certainty for financial institutions exploring digital asset services.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

body: Javier Milei had denied acting fraudulently when a cryptocurrency nosedived after he deleted a social media post about it.

articles.headline: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
body: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks. The suspected gunman has been apprehended.

articles.headline: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike

articles.headline: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
